title: The Shamash Never Rests
summary: The shamash stands up high on the menorah, all alone, and every night he runs to light another candle, and another. "Enough! I want to be a regular candle!" On the fifth night he jumps down and squeezes into the row... and suddenly nobody knows which night it is, or who will light the candles. A funny rhyming Hanukkah story with a refrain that's fun to shout: "Psss! One more light! And one more light! The shamash helps, just right!"
pages:
On the menorah, by the window, stood one candle, tall and alone.
"Why am I up here?" he grumbled. "Why not in the row like everyone?"
His name was Shamash. He was blue, and tall, and thin,
and the eight below laughed: "Shamash, Shamash, what's that grumbling? Why the grim chin?"

On the first night, Abba lit the shamash and sang a sweet song,
and the shamash hopped to one candle, hop! and back. "That's easy. That's no time long."
Then everyone looked at the little candle and clapped with delight,
and the shamash? Up there alone again. Nobody looked at him. Not one. Not quite.

On the second night, two. On the third night, three.
The shamash ran and puffed and dripped wax. Oof! What hard work for me!
Psss! One more light! And one more light! The shamash helps, just right!

On the fourth night, the shamash grumbled and stamped his foot: "Enough! I'm through! I want to be a candle!
To sit in the row and burn quietly, with nothing else to handle!"
And the little candles whispered, "Oh my, oh my... if he's a candle, who will light?"
But the shamash didn't hear. He was already hatching a plan. A sneaky one. Without blushing a mite.

On the fifth night, the shamash jumped down and squeezed in between the little candles in line:
"Move over! Move over! Now I'm in the row too!" "Ow! Ouch! Too tight!" Like sardines in a tin, packed nine.

Abba came with a match and counted, "One, two, three... nine?! Wait, wait!
Where's the shamash? Which night is it? And who will light them all? Oh, what a state!"
The children looked at the long row and sighed, "Oh... what about Hanukkah tonight?"
And the shamash felt something strange in his tummy, something heavy, like a stone, like shame, not right.

The shamash jumped, hop! up highest of all, and shouted, "Abba! I'm here! Light me, quick!"
Psss! And he ran: a candle! And another! And another! Like lightning, like a spark, lickety-split!
Psss! One more light! And one more light! The shamash helps, just right!

On the sixth night he danced. On the seventh, he did a somersault over every candle in sight!
Psss! One more light! And one more light! The shamash helps, just right! Seven! Not one mistake in sight!

And on the eighth night, eight! Psss-psss-psss... the whole row aglow!
The shamash went back up top and looked down... and suddenly saw! What a show!
Eight little lights danced beneath him, and the window, the street, and the whole city too,
because from up high, only from up high, you can see it all: every light, every house, every floor, every view.

On the menorah, by the window, stands a blue shamash, tall, and not alone.
"Why are you up there?" the candles ask. "Because from here I can see every one!"
And next year? Don't worry. He's already here, ready, shining bright:
Psss! One more light! And one more light! The shamash helps, just right!
